newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: Mauritius rupee weaker on dollar, stable on pound.
newsitem.headline: Mauritius rupee weaker on dollar, stable on pound.

text.p: The Mauritian rupee weakened against the dollar but was unchanged versus the pound on Monday, forex dealers said.
The rupee traded at a mean rate of 20.1065 against the dollar from 20.0925 last Friday. Against the pound, the rupee was fixed at a mean rate of 33.5135, unchanged from Friday.
Forex dealers said the dollar/rupee fixing took place before and did not reflect two interventions in the interbank forex market from the central bank and the Mauritius Sugar Syndicate.

The central bank was seen selling dollars to commercial banks below the prevailing interbank rate at midday Monday while the Mauritius Sugar Syndicate made a tender sale of pounds earlier during the morning.

"With the (central bank's) intervention rate well below interbank today, we are expecting the rupee to appreciate against the dollar tomorrow if the U.S. currency does not strengthen in overnight international markets," a dealer said.
The dealer said with the regular market interventions below the interbank market rate during the past few weeks, the central bank was supporting the rupee against the dollar.
Central bank governor Dan Maraye told Reuters the rupee's fixing against the dollar was reflecting the demand and offer trend on the local market.
